Data entry is a core part of using the CMS. Any time you create or update content, configure settings, or provide information, you use data‑entry fields. The most common of these is the **input field**, which allows you to type text or numbers directly into the system.

This page introduces input fields as the foundation of data entry and explains how they relate to other types of fields you may see.

## Input Fields: The Basics
Input fields are simple boxes where you can type. They are used for:
- Names, titles, and labels  
- Numbers, dates, and emails  
- Short descriptions or small amounts of text  

Because they’re so flexible, input fields appear throughout the CMS and form the base of most data‑entry tasks.

## How Input Fields Help You
- Labels tell you what information is needed  
- Placeholder text gives hints before you begin typing  
- Error messages appear if something needs to be corrected  
- Some fields expand automatically as you write more  

These features help ensure the information you enter is correct and easy to understand.

## More Than Just Text
While input fields handle most of your everyday typing, the CMS also includes other types of fields designed for specific kinds of data. These may include:
- Dropdown menus for selecting from a list  
- Toggle switches for on/off choices  
- Date or time pickers  
- Multi‑line text areas for longer content  

Input fields serve as the starting point for understanding these other components—each one simply offers a different way to provide information.
